record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Is every semi-dispersing polygon hyperbolic? Here a semi-dispersing polygon is obtained from a polygon by replacing some sides with inward-convex dispersing arcs while leaving the remaining sides neutral.

evidence.quote: ii) Всякий ли полурассеивающий многоугольник является гиперболическим?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P_0 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a (not necessarily convex) polygon with finitely many sides. A *semi-dispersing polygon* $P$ is obtained from $P_0$ by replacing a (possibly empty) subset of its straight sides by smooth arcs that are strictly convex when viewed from the interior of $P$ (i.e., dispersing/inward-convex arcs), while the remaining straight sides are kept as neutral (flat) walls. Consider the billiard flow inside $P$: a point particle moves with unit speed along straight lines and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting the boundary. The flow is called *hyperbolic* if it has nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere with respect to the natural invariant (Liouville) measure on the unit tangent bundle of $P$.

Question: Is every semi-dispersing polygon, in the sense above, hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on billiard dynamics (e.g., Chernov–Dolgopyat's survey on hyperbolic billiards and recent works on polygonal/semi-dispersing billiards) discuss hyperbolicity of semi-dispersing systems but note that long sequences of reflections without expansion can compromise hyperbolicity, and existence of Lyapunov exponents in such polygonal settings remains unresolved. No source found establishing hyperbolicity for every semi-dispersing polygon, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bridge to Hyperbolic Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Typical physical polygonal billiard is equivalent to a mathematical (point particle) semi-dispersing billiard ... hyperbolic at least on a subset of positive measure.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolicity of semi-dispersing polygonal billiards is established only on positive-measure subsets in typical cases, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Billiards and Statistical Physics (Chernov–Dolgopyat)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of hyperbolic billiards discussing semi-dispersing systems and remaining open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Full hyperbolicity of all semi-dispersing systems with neutral (flat) boundary components is not known in general.
